name: CompleteRXN Benchmark
description: CompleteRXN is a benchmark of 206,423 USPTO-derived reactions for reaction completion: given a reaction SMILES that is missing molecules, so its atoms do not balance, predict the missing molecules so that the completed reaction is balanced for atoms and charge. References come from FlowER mechanistic reactions matched to their USPTO records, with stereochemistry restored from USPTO. Three splits (random, group out-of-distribution and extreme out-of-distribution, 5 repetitions each) test generalization to increasingly unfamiliar reactions. Code, models and scoring: https://github.com/Intelligent-molecular-systems/CompleteRxn-Benchmarking

rai:dataLimitations: This benchmark is intended for chemical reaction completion on USPTO-derived reaction SMILES. It should not be interpreted as a complete or unbiased representation of all chemical reactions, all reaction conditions, or all chemistry domains. Coverage is limited by the underlying USPTO and FlowER-derived sources, extraction and canonicalization procedures, and the availability of mapped mechanistic steps. References are FlowER reactions, which may themselves be incomplete or chemically debatable for some records. Reactions whose stereochemistry could not be restored unambiguously (147) or whose input is not fully contained in the matched FlowER reaction (47) were excluded.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset may inherit selection biases from patent-derived USPTO data, including emphasis on patented, reported, and synthetically useful reactions rather than negative results, failed reactions, or unpublished chemistry. It may also inherit biases from the source datasets, reaction extraction procedures, atom mapping, canonicalization, template labels, and FlowER mechanistic-step template curation.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset consists of chemical reaction SMILES, patent numbers, years, paragraph identifiers, reaction classes, template labels and derived molecular metadata. It contains no personal or sensitive data.
rai:dataUseCases: Intended use cases include benchmarking, training, validation, and testing of models for reaction completion: given an atom-unbalanced input reaction SMILES, predict missing molecules to produce an atom- and charge-balanced reaction.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Potential positive impacts include improved reproducibility and standardization for reaction-completion models, better evaluation of chemistry-focused machine learning models, and clearer measurement of generalization under structural novelty. Potential risks include over-reliance on benchmark performance as evidence of real-world chemical competence, propagation of source-data biases.

rai:dataCollection: The benchmark is derived from public reaction datasets based on USPTO patent reactions and FlowER mechanistic reaction data. The dataset aggregates and processes existing chemical reaction records rather than collecting new data.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing includes source alignment, RDKit-based canonicalization, mapping of FlowER mechanistic steps to USPTO records, construction of imbalanced input reactions and balanced target reactions, stereo handling, calculation of missing-fragment metadata, and generation of random/group/extreme OOD split assignments.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: No manual labels are part of the benchmark dataset: inputs, references and metadata are derived computationally from USPTO curation, atom mapping, template and class labels, and FlowER mechanistic reactions. The references were audited by chemistry annotators (three graduate and four undergraduate students with completed training in organic chemistry, hired with hourly pay): 53 benchmark reactions were each completed independently by three annotators without seeing the reference and compared with it, with disagreements adjudicated by the authors. The audit cases, anonymized completions and annotation instructions are in the code repository (analysis/expert_audits).
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is versioned in its Hugging Face git repository. The completerxn package pins a repository revision and checks SHA-256 hashes of all files it downloads. Corrections will be released as new revisions with a changelog in the dataset card; issues can be reported on the GitHub repository.
